terms.grammar: adjective, third declension (present participle of īnsequor)
terms.comment: Of the day, year or time that comes next; īnsequentī annō, in the following year.

evidence: Hor. C. 1.11.8: quam minimum crēdula posterō
terms.comment: Posterō diē is “the next day”; in posterum, for the future; posterī, posterity.

evidence: Cic. Or. 21: nec acūmine posteriōrum, nec fulmine ūtēns superiōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Strictly where two are set side by side, the earlier (prior, superior) and the later.

phrases.latin: multōs vērō in terrā Umbriā ūnum et eundem diem esse dīcere ā merīdiē ad īnsequentem merīdiem
phrases.english: and that many in Umbria say one and the same day runs from noon to the following noon

sources: Lewis & Short: insequor · Lewis & Short: posterus
